_about: Single source of truth for required returns (the yearly return demanded to own a stock). Used by the full fair-value model (model/model.py), the Growth Screen and the Monthly Top 5. Order of use: stock override > theme override > sector default > default. Sector defaults = Damodaran Jan-2026 cost of equity by sector + about 1 point cushion, rounded to 0.5%, floor 7% (https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/datafile/wacc.html). Base build: risk-free ~4-4.5% + equity risk premium ~4-4.5% = ~8.5-9% for an average stock, plus company-specific risk.

small_cap_premium.reason: Added to the sector rate for the Russell 2000 screen only (scripts/build_russell.py): small companies are less diversified, less liquid and less studied, so their cash flows are less certain.

AI chips & hardware.reason: Semiconductors and AI hardware are cyclical; group default for chip stocks without their own entry below.

AAPL.reason: Mega-cap, very stable cash flows, huge buybacks: close to an average-risk stock.

MSFT.reason: Diversified software and cloud with recurring revenue and a net cash balance sheet.

GOOGL.reason: Strong balance sheet, but search faces AI disruption and regulatory risk.

AMZN.reason: Thin retail margins and very heavy AI capex make free cash flow volatile.

NVDA.reason: Below the 11.5% chip-group rate: mega-cap, net cash and a dominant position. Still above average for cyclical AI spending, customer concentration and competition. 11-12% is also defensible.

AVGO.reason: Chips plus a large recurring software business (VMware) lower the risk vs the chip group, offset by $35B net debt.

LLY.reason: Large diversified pharma; obesity-drug growth is strong but competition and pricing pressure are rising.

ADBE.reason: Recurring subscription revenue, but generative AI threatens its creative-software moat.

APP.reason: Very high margins that depend on one ad platform, short track record, regulatory and accounting scrutiny.

FICO.reason: Near-monopoly in credit scores, but pricing power is under regulatory pressure and it carries net debt.

APA.reason: Above the 8.5% Energy rate: an oil producer with Egypt and exploration risk, net debt and oil-price dependence.

DECK.reason: Fashion and brand risk (HOKA, UGG) and tariffs, partly offset by $1.1B net cash.

INCY.reason: Jakafi is ~60% of sales and loses patent protection later this decade.

MKC.reason: Below the 9% Consumer Defensive rate: spices are very stable demand. Note the pending Unilever Foods deal adds leverage risk.

EXPE.reason: Online travel agent: cyclical, and the most exposed to AI agents booking directly with hotels and airlines.

BKNG.reason: Dominant online travel platform with strong direct traffic; travel is cyclical and AI agents are a new disintermediation risk.

INTU.reason: Sticky TurboTax / QuickBooks franchises, but AI tax and bookkeeping agents are a real threat to pricing power.

ADSK.reason: Design software with high switching costs; exposed to construction and manufacturing cycles and AI-native design tools.

TPR.reason: Fashion brand (Coach) risk and tariffs; store leases add leverage.

VEEV.reason: Mission-critical life-sciences software with large net cash; risk from Salesforce competition in CRM.

MNST.reason: Below the 9% Consumer Defensive rate: very stable demand, no debt, long growth record.

ALLE.reason: Steady locks and access-control business; tied to the non-residential construction cycle, moderate debt.

FTNT.reason: Cybersecurity is durable demand, but firewall hardware refresh cycles make growth lumpy.

RMD.reason: Healthcare device leader with recurring masks revenue; GLP-1 drugs are a long-term demand risk.

V.reason: Above the 7.5% financials rate: payment networks are very durable but face regulation and new payment rails.

MA.reason: Above the 7.5% financials rate: payment networks are very durable but face regulation and new payment rails.

FIX.reason: Construction contractor at a cyclical peak driven by AI data-centre spending; earnings can fall fast if that slows.

CTAS.reason: Very steady recurring uniform and facility services with a long record; slightly below the 9% industrials rate.

DXCM.reason: Growing device market but strong Abbott competition, pricing pressure and recent product-quality issues.

IDXX.reason: Recurring veterinary test revenue and a strong installed base; sensitive to vet-visit volumes.

VRSN.reason: Regulated near-monopoly (.com/.net registry) with very stable cash flows; risk is contract and price-cap changes.

NDAQ.reason: Durable exchange and fintech franchise, but high debt from the Adenza deal.

MCO.reason: Ratings duopoly with high margins; revenue swings with bond issuance.

SPGI.reason: Ratings, indices and data with wide moats; pro-forma figures after the Mobility spin-off add some uncertainty.

NFLX.reason: Global streaming leader, but competition for viewing time, content costs and ad growth add risk.

CBOE.reason: Options-exchange franchise with net cash; volumes and revenue swing with market volatility.

GRMN.reason: Diversified device maker with no debt and a long record; consumer spending is cyclical.

FDS.reason: Sticky subscription data business, but AI could commoditise financial data and research tools.

CRM.reason: Leading CRM platform, but heavy new debt for buybacks and AI agents threaten seat-based pricing.

HWM.reason: Strong position in engine parts, but aerospace is cyclical and it carries net debt.

ADP.reason: Very steady payroll franchise with a long record; sensitive to employment and interest rates.

AME.reason: Steady diversified industrial with a long record of acquisitions; moderate debt.

AXP.reason: Premium card issuer and network: durable brand, but it lends, so credit losses rise in recessions.

SHOP.reason: Fast-growing commerce platform priced for continued high growth; very volatile shares (beta ~2.6).

PYPL.reason: Large digital wallet with slowing growth and competition at checkout from Apple Pay and others.

ADYEY.reason: High-quality global acquirer with net cash, but growth swings with large merchants; euro-reported (FX risk for USD holders).

FISV.reason: Sticky bank-technology franchise, but heavy debt and a recent guidance reset.

CRCL.reason: Young public company; income depends on interest rates, USDC adoption and crypto regulation.

SPG.reason: Leveraged mall REIT: steady rents, but $28B of debt makes the equity sensitive to rates and retail health.

META.reason: Dominant ad platforms and net cash, but record AI capex and regulatory risk.

TT.reason: Leading HVAC franchise; cyclical end-markets offset by services and data-centre demand.

RL.reason: Strong brand, but fashion cycles, tariffs and discretionary spending.

ROST.reason: Consistent off-price retailer with net-cash-like balance sheet; thin margins.

GDDY.reason: Very cash-generative, but low growth and AI disruption risk to website building.

FAST.reason: High-quality distributor, little debt; exposed to the industrial cycle.

SYK.reason: Diversified med-tech leader with steady growth; some acquisition debt.

CMG.reason: Strong unit growth, but restaurant traffic and food costs swing.

KLAC.reason: Process-control leader with high margins, but semiconductor equipment is cyclical.

CME.reason: Near-monopoly futures exchange with very high margins and low beta; volumes vary with volatility.

STE.reason: Recurring sterilisation consumables and services; defensive.

WDAY.reason: Sticky enterprise software, but heavy stock pay and AI seat-count risk.

BR.reason: Mostly recurring, contract-based revenue in a near-monopoly (proxy processing).

MSI.reason: Sticky public-safety customers and large backlog; acquisition debt.

BKR.reason: Energy-cycle exposure and new acquisition debt, partly offset by gas/LNG technology.

RSG.reason: Essential, regulated-like waste service with pricing power; very low beta.

WAB.reason: Rail equipment leader with backlog; cyclical rail capex.

MRVL.reason: Fast-growing but very volatile; depends on a few hyperscaler AI programmes.

LULU.reason: Strong brand with net-cash-like balance sheet, but US sales shrinking under competition.

RDDT.reason: Young, fast-growing ad platform; very volatile and dependent on search traffic and AI licensing.

CF.reason: Low-cost producer, but nitrogen prices are cyclical.

EME.reason: Well-run contractor near a cyclical peak in data-centre construction.

HST.reason: Low-leverage hotel REIT; lodging demand is cyclical.

LII.reason: Leading HVAC brand; housing and replacement cycles.

NEM.reason: Diversified gold miner; value moves with the gold price.

REGN.reason: Profitable biotech with net cash; drug pricing, biosimilar and pipeline risk.

ZTS.reason: Defensive animal-health leader; growth has slowed.

MO.reason: Very steady cash flows, but a declining product and regulatory/litigation risk.

HAS.reason: Toy demand is cyclical; Wizards of the Coast adds a profitable digital franchise.

BMY.reason: Large, low-beta pharma facing a patent cliff around 2028.

NRG.reason: Heavy debt and thin, commodity-linked margins; data-centre power upside.

FIS.reason: Integration of a large acquisition and high debt.

PG.reason: Below the 9% Consumer Defensive rate: household staples with very stable demand and a beta near 0.4.

KO.reason: Below the 9% Consumer Defensive rate: global beverage brand with very stable demand and a beta near 0.3.

SHW.reason: Below the 9.5% Basic Materials rate: paint is less cyclical than chemicals (repaint demand), but tied to housing and industry.

JNJ.reason: Below the 9% Healthcare rate: AAA balance sheet, diversified drugs and devices, beta near 0.2.

AMGN.reason: Slightly below the 9% Healthcare rate: large, low-beta biotech, but biosimilar erosion and $54B of debt.

VLTO.reason: Below the 9% Industrials rate: water-quality consumables and service make most revenue recurring; beta near 0.7 and modest debt.

AMP.reason: Above the 7.5% Financial Services rate: fees move with stock and bond markets (beta ~1.1) and it carries an annuity and life-insurance book.

PPG.reason: Basic Materials rate: coatings demand follows the industrial and auto cycle, with net debt of about 2x EBITDA.

EOG.reason: Above the 8.5% Energy rate: oil-price dependent, but a low-cost producer with little net debt.

PM.reason: Below the 9% Consumer Defensive rate: very steady cash flows (beta ~0.35), offset by regulation, excise and currency risk and high debt.

DLTR.reason: Consumer Defensive rate: steady discount demand, but execution risk in the multi-price rollout and tariff exposure.

INVA.reason: Healthcare rate (9%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium: steady royalty cash, but the GSK inhaler royalties end within the decade.

CTRE.reason: Real Estate rate (7.5%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium: long leases, but tenants are thin-margin nursing operators paid by Medicaid and Medicare.

CVSA.reason: Consumer Defensive rate (9%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium: steady demand for nurses and doctors, offset by US student-aid rule risk.

QLYS.reason: Technology rate (10.5%) less half a point for recurring subscriptions, net cash and low beta (~0.5), plus the 2-point small-cap premium.

LAUR.reason: Consumer Defensive rate (9%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium, plus 1 point for Mexican and Peruvian currency and politics.

IDCC.reason: Technology rate (10.5%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium: licence income depends on renewals and litigation with a few large phone makers (beta ~1.5).

LMAT.reason: Healthcare rate (9%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium: niche vascular devices with steady demand, net cash.

BOX.reason: Technology rate (10.5%) less half a point for recurring subscriptions and low beta (~0.6), plus the 2-point small-cap premium.

ACIW.reason: Technology rate (10.5%) less half a point for long bank contracts, plus the 2-point small-cap premium; lumpy licence sales and net debt.

ALL.reason: Financial Services rate (7.5%) plus 1.5 points for an underwriter's catastrophe exposure (wildfires, hurricanes, storms) and swings in auto claim costs.

HIG.reason: Financial Services rate (7.5%) plus 1 point for underwriting risk; mostly commercial lines and group benefits, so less catastrophe-exposed than a home insurer.

AIZ.reason: Financial Services rate (7.5%) plus 1.5 points: protection plans are steady, but Global Housing is exposed to hurricanes.

MRSH.reason: Above the 7.5% Financial Services rate: a broker takes no underwriting risk and earns steady fees (beta ~0.5), but carries $22B of debt after the McGriff deal and consulting is cyclical. In line with ADP and BR.

WTW.reason: Above the 7.5% Financial Services rate: broking and consulting fees with no underwriting risk (beta ~0.4); net debt and pension-consulting cycles. In line with ADP and BR.

NMIH.reason: Financial Services rate (7.5%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium, plus half a point: mortgage-insurance losses come all at once in a housing downturn.

UVE.reason: Financial Services rate (7.5%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium, plus 2.5 points: almost all risk is Florida homes, so one major hurricane can wipe out years of profit.

PLMR.reason: Financial Services rate (7.5%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium, plus 1 point for earthquake and other catastrophe exposure and fast growth.

PLGO.reason: Financial Services rate (7.5%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium, plus 1.5 points for (re)insurance catastrophe risk, a short listed history and few analysts.

CRVL.reason: Financial Services rate (7.5%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium: fee-based claims services with no underwriting risk and net cash.

SLDE.reason: Financial Services rate (7.5%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium, plus 2.5 points: Florida hurricane concentration and a record of only four years, none with a major storm on its book.

HG.reason: Financial Services rate (7.5%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium, plus 1 point for reinsurance catastrophe risk and a cyclical market.

HCI.reason: Financial Services rate (7.5%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium, plus 2.5 points: almost all risk is Florida homes (Hurricane Ian cost a third of its book value in 2022).

ESNT.reason: Financial Services rate (7.5%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium, plus half a point: mortgage-insurance losses come all at once in a housing downturn.

UFCS.reason: Financial Services rate (7.5%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium, plus half a point for a long record of reserve charges and a young turnaround.

SKWD.reason: Financial Services rate (7.5%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium, plus half a point for casualty reserve risk and integrating the Apollo business.

QQQ.reason: Nasdaq-100 basket: diversified but tech-heavy, so slightly above an average stock.

CPRT.reason: Industrials rate: salvage-auction volumes are steady (cars get wrecked in any economy) and it holds $4.4B net cash, but fees follow used-car prices and insurers' total-loss rates.

AOS.reason: Industrials rate: about 80% of North American water-heater sales are replacements, which steadies demand; China (a fifth of sales) is weak and housing-linked.

TPL.reason: Above the 8.5% Energy rate: royalties carry no drilling cost and there is no debt, but income depends on oil and gas prices and on drilling in one basin (the Permian).

VICI.reason: Real Estate rate (7.5%) plus 1 point: 40-year inflation-linked leases, but two tenants (Caesars and MGM) pay about three quarters of the rent and $17.8B of debt makes the equity sensitive to rates.

LIN.reason: Below the 9.5% Basic Materials rate: industrial gases are sold on 10-20 year take-or-pay contracts with price escalators, beta ~0.7; offset by $23B net debt.

CL.reason: Below the 9% Consumer Defensive rate: toothpaste, soap and pet food with very stable demand and a beta near 0.3 (as for PG and KO).

ALGN.reason: Healthcare rate (9%) plus 1 point: clear aligners are an elective purchase that follows consumer confidence (beta ~1.7), with rising low-price competition; net cash.

ANET.reason: Below the 11.5% chip-and-hardware group rate: $14B net cash, no debt and the leading position in data-centre switching; still depends on a few hyperscalers' AI spending (Microsoft and Meta are about 40% of sales).

WSM.reason: Consumer Cyclical rate (9%) plus half a point: home furnishings follow housing turnover and are exposed to tariffs (beta ~1.5); no borrowings.

LRN.reason: Consumer Defensive rate (9%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium, plus 1 point: revenue is public school funding paid through state and charter contracts, which politics can change.

MCRI.reason: Consumer Cyclical rate (9%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium: two casinos only (Reno and Black Hawk), so local competition or regulation matters, but no borrowings.

CARG.reason: Communication Services rate (9%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium, plus half a point: dealer advertising follows the car market (beta ~1.2).

USLM.reason: Basic Materials rate (9.5%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium, less half a point: no debt, $0.4B cash and local lime markets with few rivals; demand follows construction, steel and oil and gas.

EPAC.reason: Industrials rate (9%) plus the 2-point small-cap premium: leading brand in a niche, low debt, but orders follow industrial, energy and infrastructure spending.
